research_notes: Second named Swiss university, fetched to show the fee model is not uniform. UZH uses a base tuition plus an explicit foreign-student surcharge, whereas ETH uses a threefold multiplier for non-qualifying third-country students (see 001_bachelor_tuition.json). A third-country Bachelor student at UZH therefore pays CHF 720 + CHF 500 = CHF 1,220 per semester of tuition plus the CHF 59 mandatory semester contributions, i.e. CHF 1,279 per semester and CHF 2,558 for two semesters, plus a non-refundable application fee of CHF 150 for applicants with foreign qualifications. Note the tuition-fee components and the contributions are billed as distinct items and the CHF 2,558 figure is an arithmetic sum of the page's own numbers, not a figure printed on the page.

claims.statement: The University of Zurich charges a tuition fee of CHF 720 per semester for students, plus a surcharge of CHF 500 per semester for foreign students at Bachelor level.
claims.unit: CHF per semester (base tuition, foreign Bachelor surcharge of CHF 500 additional)

claims.statement: The University of Zurich adds mandatory semester contributions totalling CHF 59, made up of a scholarship fund contribution of CHF 6.50, libraries and collections CHF 15, academic sport CHF 35 and student concerns CHF 2.50.

The University of Zurich charges applicants with foreign qualifications an application fee of CHF 150, applicable from 1 January 2025, and states that application fees are not refunded or credited against other fees.
